tEn: Jensen Huang on AI Capex, 2027 Bottlenecks, and the Singularity
tZh: 黄仁勋谈 AI 资本支出、2027 年瓶颈与奇点
sEn: Jensen Huang discusses whether AI revenue justifies capex, the bottlenecks coming in 2027, the singularity, and the open vs closed AI debate.
sZh: 黄仁勋探讨 AI 收入能否支撑资本支出、2027 年将出现的瓶颈、奇点以及开源与闭源 AI 之争。

consensus.en: Functionality, capability, safety, and security are inseparable and must be accelerated together.
consensus.zh: 功能性、能力、安全与安保密不可分，必须同步加速推进。

consensus.en: The age of agents is here; coding was the first on-ramp, now design, science, and physical AI follow.
consensus.zh: 智能体时代已经到来；编程是第一个入口，如今设计、科学与具身 AI 紧随其后。

consensus.en: Compute demand will grow a billion times because thinking and reasoning require vastly more inference.
consensus.zh: 算力需求将增长十亿倍，因为思考与推理需要远超以往的推理量。

consensus.en: Containment, out-of-band monitoring, and zero-trust access are essential for safe autonomous systems.
consensus.zh: 遏制、带外监控与零信任访问是安全自主系统不可或缺的要素。

consensus.en: Physical AI is a massive opportunity; every industry touching the physical world will be reinvented.
consensus.zh: 具身 AI 是巨大机遇；每一个触及物理世界的行业都将被重塑。

consensus.en: The U.S. must attract global talent; immigration is America's superpower for innovation.
consensus.zh: 美国必须吸引全球人才；移民是美国创新的超级力量。

contrarian.en: Perfect alignment is impossible; containment and monitoring, not alignment, ensure safety.
contrarian.zh: 完美对齐不可能实现；确保安全的是遏制与监控，而非对齐。

contrarian.en: AI will not give us more leisure; it will unlock more ambition and opportunity.
contrarian.zh: AI 不会给我们更多闲暇；它将释放更多雄心与机遇。

contrarian.en: Moore's law is over; doubling transistors now costs double, not the same price.
contrarian.zh: 摩尔定律已终结；如今晶体管数量翻倍，成本也翻倍，而非价格不变。

contrarian.en: We put too much pressure on two labs; a third of compute is general purpose, a third startups.
contrarian.zh: 我们给两家实验室施加了太多压力；三分之一算力用于通用计算，三分之一用于初创公司。

contrarian.en: Nvidia's moat is increasing with scale; specialization is the enemy of fungibility and durability.
contrarian.zh: 英伟达的护城河随规模扩大而加深；专业化是通用性与耐久性的敌人。

contrarian.en: Doom predictions underestimate human capacity; smart people solve problems without central direction.
contrarian.zh: 末日预测低估了人类能力；聪明人无需中央指挥也能解决问题。

turns.en: This is an existential issue for us. We could easily stop, but if we stop today, we lose. Functionality, capability, safety, security—they're all at exactly the same place. Priority number one.
turns.zh: 这对我们来说是一个生存问题。我们很容易停下来，但如果我们今天停下来，我们就输了。功能性、能力、安全性、保障——它们都处在完全相同的位置。头等大事。

turns.en: It's our third pod back together.
turns.zh: 这是我们第三次一起做播客了。

turns.en: In the last 10 days, you've been at the state dinner at the White House. You were at the White House summit where we did the accord on superintelligence, and just yesterday you were there with your parents when the president presented you with the National Medal of Science.
turns.zh: 在过去 10 天里，你出席了白宫的国宴。你参加了白宫峰会，我们在那里签署了关于超级智能的协议，而就在昨天，你和你的父母一起在那里，总统向你颁发了国家科学奖章。

turns.en: You were the only investor at the table.
turns.zh: 你是唯一一位与会的投资者。

turns.en: You were the only investor at the table, now that we reflected on it.
turns.zh: 现在回想起来，你是唯一一位与会的投资者。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Well, tell me about being there with your parents yesterday.
turns.zh: 那跟我说说昨天和你父母一起在那里的情况吧。

turns.en: Right, it struck me—five out of the six people on stage were all born outside of the United States. How did that feel?
turns.zh: 对，让我印象深刻的是——台上六个人中有五个都出生在美国以外。那是什么感觉？

turns.en: Well, first of all, it's a great honor all by itself, right? And it's a reflection of the contribution that the company has made, right? And obviously, we created—we invented a new computing model. This is probably the most pervasive computing model in the world today. It's the only computing architecture that's in every cloud. It's in every computer company. It's used in every field of science. It's used by gamers. It's used by creators and builders, and it's used by scientists. It powers intelligence, right? I mean, just if you take a step back and you look at what the company has accomplished—we started out building a graphics chip for gamers, and I'm still proud of that, of course. And we now shipped 1.67 billion units, right? That's how many generations of—I mean, I raised generations of scientists and kids and designers, you know. And so I think the impact—and here we are, we're the infrastructure that powers the intelligence of society. So it's an incredibly proud moment for me to receive the award on behalf of the company. Now for my parents, I wanted them to go, and I gave them literally 24 hours lead time, and they don't travel that much, right? They don't travel that much. And my dad didn't even have a suit.
turns.zh: 嗯，首先，这本身就是极大的荣誉，对吧？这也反映了公司所做的贡献，对吧？显然，我们创造——我们发明了一种新的计算模型。这可能是当今世界上应用最广泛的计算模型。它是唯一一种存在于每个云中的计算架构。它存在于每家计算机公司。它被用于每个科学领域。它被游戏玩家使用。它被创作者和构建者使用，也被科学家使用。它驱动智能，对吧？我的意思是，如果你退一步看看公司取得的成就——我们最初是为游戏玩家制造图形芯片，当然我至今仍为此感到自豪。我们现在已经出货了 16.7 亿台，对吧？我培养了几代科学家、孩子和设计师。所以我认为其影响——现在我们就是驱动社会智能的基础设施。因此，代表公司获得这个奖项对我来说是无比自豪的时刻。至于我的父母，我想让他们去，我给了他们仅仅 24 小时的通知时间，他们不太常旅行，对吧？他们不太常旅行。我父亲甚至没有一套西装。

turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.en: Yeah. So he ran out and bought a suit. And he looked great. They looked great.
turns.zh: 是的。所以他跑出去买了一套西装。他看起来很棒。他们看起来很棒。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: It was a brand new suit and he showed up. I didn't realize he had a suit. I thought he was just going to wear some shirt. And he went out and bought a suit. My mom got a new dress, literally in 24 hours.
turns.zh: 那是一套全新的西装，他出现了。我没想到他有西装。我以为他只会穿件衬衫。他出去买了一套西装。我妈妈买了一条新裙子，真的就在 24 小时内。

turns.en: Yeah. Oh, I know how it works.
turns.zh: 是的。哦，我知道那是怎么回事。

turns.en: Oh my gosh. It's incredible. And so we got them on a—we chartered a plane for them, got them there, and they were so happy to meet the president. And President Trump walked my mom—because she has a hard time walking—and the two of them were walking off stage and he held her and walked her down the stage, and they were just incredibly proud to meet him. But for them, it's their American dream. You know, my dad—I still remember, I think I was like 5 years old or something like that. And he had just come back from the United States on a business trip. He was working for an air conditioning company.
turns.zh: 哦，天哪。太不可思议了。所以我们让他们——我们为他们包了一架飞机，把他们送到那里，他们非常高兴见到总统。特朗普总统扶着我妈妈——因为她走路困难——他们两人一起走下舞台，他扶着她，带她走下舞台，他们非常自豪能见到他。但对他们来说，这是他们的美国梦。你知道，我爸爸——我还记得，我想我当时大概 5 岁左右。他刚从美国出差回来。他在一家空调公司工作。

turns.en: And you were living in Taiwan.
turns.zh: 当时你们住在台湾。

turns.en: We were—at the time we had just moved to Thailand. Thailand.
turns.zh: 我们——当时我们刚搬到泰国。泰国。

turns.en: Oh no, no, we were just about to move to Thailand. And we were in Taiwan. He had come back—
turns.zh: 哦不，不，我们正要搬到泰国。当时我们在台湾。他回来了——

turns.en: He was in the United States working for a company called Carrier, an air conditioning company. And he was here for training. And of all the places in the world, they landed him in New York.
turns.zh: 他在美国为一家叫开利的公司工作，一家空调公司。他来这里是接受培训。世界上那么多地方，他们偏偏把他送到了纽约。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.en: And so here you can just imagine—a kid in the late 20s, I guess mid-late 20s, and never been outside of Taiwan, goes to United States, New York City of all places. And he saw the future of the future. And he came back, you know, mind-blown, all the things that he bought at the airport brought it back. He bought chocolate. He brought that cheese that you have in a tube back in the old days. It's kind of like white strange cheese. It comes in a tube.
turns.zh: 所以你可以想象——一个 20 多岁的小伙子，我想是 25 到 29 岁左右，从未离开过台湾，去了美国，偏偏是纽约市。他看到了未来的未来。他回来时，你知道，被震撼了，他在机场买的所有东西都带了回来。他买了巧克力。他带了那种老式管装奶酪。有点像白色的奇怪奶酪。它装在管子里。

turns.en: It's great.
turns.zh: 很棒。

turns.en: And he brought back all kinds of strange things. And he says, 'This is—we should go there someday.' And the first opportunity they had, they sent my older brother and I to the United States. And you know, it was his dream. I don't think many people realize that you came to the United States ahead of your parents.
turns.zh: 他带回了各种奇怪的东西。他说：‘这——我们有一天应该去那里。’他们一有机会，就把我和我哥哥送到了美国。你知道，这是他的梦想。我想很多人没有意识到你比你的父母先来到美国。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Right. And they joined a few years later, but it just hit me like a ton of bricks that five out of the six people on that stage yesterday were born outside the United States. You and I have talked about the need for—with all the other stuff going on—a real strategy and an immigration policy that makes certain that we're still the place that all the great builders in the world want to come build. This is America's superpower, right? In a lot of ways, the intellectual property creation capability of our nation is unlike anything else in the world. And the reason for that is we attract the world's best. That's right. You know, we are the place where they want to come and build their lives because of the opportunity it provides, the freedom that she offers, the opportunity that it provides, the spirit of invention and entrepreneurialism and the can-do attitude. You know, in the United States, everything is possible.
turns.zh: 对。他们几年后也来了，但昨天台上六个人中有五个出生在美国以外，这让我深受震撼。你和我讨论过，在所有其他事情发生的情况下，我们需要一个真正的战略和移民政策，确保我们仍然是世界上所有伟大的建设者都想来建设的地方。这是美国的超级力量，对吧？在很多方面，我们国家的知识产权创造能力是世界上独一无二的。原因就是我们吸引了世界上最优秀的人才。没错。你知道，我们是他们想要来建立生活的地方，因为它提供的机遇、它提供的自由、它提供的可能性、发明和创业精神以及‘我能行’的态度。你知道，在美国，一切皆有可能。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: We start with 'of course it's possible, of course we could do that' instead of—I do a lot of travel—'of course you can't do that, of course' in other places. And we take it for granted. But the spirit, the energy that comes around with the culture that we've created here—it just can't be understated. And so I think the inflow of intellectual property into this country is unlike anything else the world's ever seen.
turns.zh: 我们从‘当然可能，当然我们可以做到’开始，而不是——我经常旅行——在其他地方是‘当然你做不到，当然’。我们把这视为理所当然。但这里创造的文化所带来的精神、能量——怎么强调都不为过。所以我认为流入这个国家的知识产权是世界上前所未有的。

turns.en: It's true.
turns.zh: 确实如此。

turns.en: And we want that. We want all of the world's great minds to come here, bring their great ideas, make them realize them here.
turns.zh: 我们想要这样。我们希望世界上所有伟大的头脑都来这里，带来他们伟大的想法，在这里实现它们。

turns.en: Realize them here and let us keep that flywheel going.
turns.zh: 在这里实现它们，让我们保持这个飞轮转动。

turns.en: You know, I really—it's a delicate system. It's a delicate balance. I get it's a delicate balance. And so we have to do it lawfully. You have to do it rightfully, right? But we surely want to do it.
turns.zh: 你知道，我真的——这是一个微妙的系统。这是一个微妙的平衡。我明白这是一个微妙的平衡。所以我们必须合法地做。必须正当地做，对吧？但我们当然想这样做。

turns.en: Yeah, for sure.
turns.zh: 是的，当然。

turns.en: So, I want to start high level just kind of where we are. Then I want to dig down a little bit into the safety and regulation and getting this right, where we are in terms of the compute buildout. And then finally, we're going to finish up drilling in a little bit to Nvidia's growth and what's going on there. But you've been really good at calling the future, right? Two years ago, we were sitting here and you said that the market was dramatically underestimating the amount of compute buildout that was going to be required and was going to happen over the course of the next five years. You said it's not going to be a trillion, it's going to be two trillion at a minimum in terms of cumulative compute buildout. And of course, now we're over that. You said before everybody was thinking about it that inference, right, compute was going to 1 billionx because of inference time reasoning and thinking. And then last year, of course, before we saw Opus 4.6, before we saw Claude Code, you said we're entering the age of agents, right, where we're going to unlock a lot of these capabilities. And of course, we saw Opus 4.6 and Claude Code really took off. So, where are we now?
turns.zh: 所以，我想先从宏观层面开始，谈谈我们现在所处的位置。然后我想深入探讨一下安全和监管，以及如何把这件事做对，还有我们在算力建设方面的进展。最后，我们会稍微深入一下 Nvidia 的增长和那边的情况。但你一直很擅长预测未来，对吧？两年前，我们坐在这里，你说市场严重低估了未来五年所需的算力建设规模。你说不会是 1 万亿，至少会是 2 万亿的累计算力建设。当然，现在我们已经超过了。在所有人还没想到的时候，你就说推理——算力会因为推理时的思考而增长 10 亿倍。然后去年，当然，在我们看到 Opus 4.6 之前，在我们看到 Claude Code 之前，你说我们正在进入智能体的时代，对吧，我们将解锁很多这些能力。当然，我们看到了 Opus 4.6 和 Claude Code 真的起飞了。那么，我们现在在哪里？

turns.en: Right, we have Elon and Sam and only three things that I said that came true. There's another 200. Why don't you just keep that? Let's just let that be the podcast.
turns.zh: 对，我们有 Elon 和 Sam，而我说过的事情只有三件成真了。还有另外 200 件呢。你为什么不保留那个？就让那成为播客吧。

turns.en: So, our investor day in a couple weeks is on entering the singularity, this acceleration. We have Elon and Sam and Demis all say, "Hey, we're in the foothills or entering the singularity." We have model solving Navier Stokes as you know. So when you look into your crystal ball where are we and are we inflecting are we accelerating into a different phase of super intelligence.
turns.zh: 所以，我们几周后的投资者日是关于进入奇点，这种加速。我们有 Elon、Sam 和 Demis 都说，“嘿，我们正在山脚下或正在进入奇点。”我们有模型解决 Navier-Stokes 方程，如你所知。那么，当你看向你的水晶球时，我们在哪里，我们是在拐点，是在加速进入超级智能的不同阶段吗？

turns.en: Let's unpack that first. First of all it's very fairly logical why the amount of compute that we're going to need is a billion times more than where we were just recently, say last year. And the reason for that is because thinking and problem solving takes a lot more inferences than repeating something, regurgitating something that you memorized.
turns.zh: 让我们先解开这一点。首先，为什么我们需要的算力会比我们最近，比如去年，多 10 亿倍，这非常合乎逻辑。原因在于，思考和解决问题比重复、 regurgitating 你记住的东西需要更多的推理。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: So when you're a ChatGPT, you give it a prompt, most of that knowledge was encoded into the large language model. Unfortunately, of course, it hallucinated and so the next click was it was generative, but it was also grounded or conditioned by ground truth.
turns.zh: 所以当你使用 ChatGPT 时，你给它一个提示，大部分知识都编码在大语言模型中。不幸的是，当然，它会幻觉，所以下一步是生成，但也基于或受限于真实数据。

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And so it would have to go out and do a search, do a quick search, comes back with the ground truth, and then from that conditioning augmented with its own what it already learned pre-training and it would generate new whatever the answer is. Well, most of the things that we want to really do that are interesting requires you to reason step by step to come up with several options plan and you might decide let's see how these things all roll out and then based on the answers of all of those I reflect on the best answer so far the best path so far I might choose one or two or three of them roll them out.
turns.zh: 所以它必须出去搜索，快速搜索，带回真实数据，然后从那种条件中，加上它自己在预训练中已经学到的东西，它会生成新的答案。嗯，我们真正想做的有趣的事情大多需要你逐步推理，想出几个选项计划，你可能会决定让我们看看这些如何展开，然后基于所有这些答案，我反思到目前为止最好的答案，最好的路径，我可能选择一两个或三个，展开它们。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: Okay prune the rest of it and then you just keep on doing this and you know people we do this that's the reason why we say great strategists love strategic optionality. You don't want to prune things too fast on the one hand, but you also have to optimize your resources. Well, AIs are doing that. Okay. So they're keeping their strategic optionality. They're rolling things out. They're pruning. They're reflecting, they're pruning, so on and so forth. All of that thinking, all of that exploration just takes a lot more compute and not on top of that because it's able to now do productive things, we're going to use it for more things. And so the compounding of both it uses more compute to do its job, but it's doing a good job and therefore we're going to apply we're going to hire it to do more jobs.
turns.zh: 好，修剪其余的，然后你继续这样做，你知道人们我们这样做，这就是为什么我们说伟大的战略家喜欢战略选择权。一方面你不想太快修剪东西，但你也必须优化你的资源。嗯，AI 正在这样做。好。所以它们保持战略选择权。它们展开东西。它们修剪。它们反思，它们修剪，等等。所有这些思考，所有这些探索都需要更多的算力，而且不仅如此，因为它现在能够做生产性的事情，我们会用它做更多事情。所以两者复合：它使用更多算力来完成工作，但它做得很好，因此我们会应用，我们会雇佣它做更多工作。

turns.en: Exactly.
turns.zh: 正是如此。

turns.en: Okay. And so that all compounds. At this point I would say that the big observation from last year is that on the one hand we want the models to get better and better and we still want the models to get better and the scaling laws of models are going to continue. However, the attachment of a harness, basically the exoskeleton of the large language model, right?
turns.zh: 好。所以这一切都复合。在这一点上，我会说去年的重大观察是，一方面我们希望模型越来越好，我们仍然希望模型变得更好，模型的缩放定律将继续。然而，附加一个框架，基本上是大语言模型的外骨骼，对吧？

turns.en: You know, kind of the body of the brain.
turns.zh: 你知道，有点像大脑的身体。

turns.en: That allows it to manage working memory, manage knowledge. How do you go from working memory to short-term to long term to basically formulating your knowledge graph, which is what we all do? we kind of think about, hey, you know, what did I learn and how does it fit into everything that I know in the past and you know how when we go to bed we do compaction things that don't make sense we kind of or don't matter we kind of eventually forget but the things that kind of matter somehow it gets reconnected and so we're doing that kind of offline and so we got working memory we have offline knowledge extraction and creation knowledge graph creation that whole part of memory is a big deal the other thing is of course tool use and we've taught these tools these AIs how to interact with the most important tools that the humans have ever made. We should accelerate that." It's all part of the same thing. You can't separate capability, functionality from safety and security. They go as one.
turns.zh: 对吧？如果你现在问我，我想每个人都会说，“让我们加速安保。让我们加速安全技术。”没有人说，“不，让我们放慢那个，对吧？我们应该加速那个。”这都是同一件事的一部分。你不能将能力、功能与安全和安保分开。它们是一体的。

turns.en: And when you deliver the service, nobody's going to say, you know, good, good, you know, I really like the functionality of your service, but boy, is it, you know, wrecking havoc. And so I think it's all one thing and we treat it as all one thing and the industry has to treat it as one thing and when we say accelerate we have to mean accelerating the entire package and right now including the safety.
turns.zh: 当你提供服务时，没有人会说，你知道，好，好，你知道，我真的很喜欢你的服务的功能，但是天哪，它，你知道，正在造成严重破坏。所以我认为这都是一件事，我们把它当作一件事来对待，行业必须把它当作一件事来对待，当我说加速时，我们必须意味着加速整个包，现在包括安全。

turns.en: Including especially the safety.
turns.zh: 包括尤其是安全。

turns.en: You mentioned pacing um especially safety.
turns.zh: 你提到了节奏，嗯，尤其是安全。

turns.en: You know, some people read Pacing the Frontier by Dario and thought that meant slowing down. And I thought a funny moment in the room was when the president called on his new best friend Dario. He referred to him in that way and he said, you know, explain to me, you know, your version of fast and safe. And Dario started off by saying, Mr. President, you said whoever wins AI wins, right? And he said that we're all speeding up, that they're speeding up, that they want to go fast, that they want to, you know, win the race with China, but also acknowledge that along the way, just to your point you just made, we have to make sure the safety systems are also speeding up and also keeping pace.
turns.zh: 你知道，有些人读了 Dario 的《Pacing the Frontier》，认为那意味着放慢速度。我认为房间里一个有趣的时刻是总统叫他的新好朋友 Dario。他用那种方式称呼他，他说，你知道，向我解释一下，你知道，你的快速和安全版本。Dario 一开始说，总统先生，你说谁赢得人工智能谁就赢，对吧？他说我们都在加速，他们也在加速，他们想快速前进，他们想，你知道，赢得与中国的竞赛，但也承认，一路上，正如你刚才指出的，我们必须确保安全系统也在加速，也在保持同步。

turns.en: So, I thought that was an important moment where you had, you know, because I think people have positioned him as though he's in opposition, right, to this, but it seemed to me that you were all very much on the same page. You went to the cabinet room with him and Greg and the other frontier labs to sign this agreement. Was there any chatter in that room about differences of opinion, or was everybody—obviously you got it signed. Did anybody have to be put in a headlock, or did everybody go willingly?
turns.zh: 所以我觉得那是一个重要的时刻，因为我认为人们把他定位成好像反对这件事，对吧，但在我看来你们其实非常一致。你和他、Greg 以及其他前沿实验室的人一起去内阁会议室签了这份协议。那个房间里有没有关于意见分歧的议论，还是说大家——显然你们把它签下来了。有没有人需要被强行按住，还是大家都是自愿的？

turns.en: No, everybody was very constructive, very productive. And I think that, without exception, everybody is dedicated to advancing the industry safely and securely. And the reason for that is because if it's not safe, if it's not secure, the functionality will never get a chance to speak. And so the capability will never get a chance to shine. And so we know that the priorities are at all times safety and security.
turns.zh: 不，每个人都非常有建设性、非常高效。我认为无一例外，每个人都致力于安全、可靠地推进这个行业。原因在于，如果不安全、不可靠，功能就永远没有机会发声，能力也永远没有机会闪耀。所以我们知道，任何时候的首要任务都是安全和可靠。

turns.en: Of course, recognizing that this industry came through a transition just recently, right? It wasn't but six months ago—this technology barely worked.
turns.zh: 当然，要认识到这个行业刚刚经历了一次转变，对吧？就在六个月前——这项技术还几乎不能用。

turns.en: Exactly. And so without functionality and capability, what's the point in making it safe and secure? Nobody even cares about it. And so obviously the first job of AI is to demonstrate it could do something useful, right? And it really reached that point six months ago. And so now it really wants to be deployed and broadly deployed. And so there's no question that the entire industry now has a strategic imperative, an incredible imperative and great urgency, to make sure that whatever we deploy is safe and secure. And so I think everybody is completely convinced: capability, functionality, safety, security—they're all at exactly the same place.
turns.zh: 正是如此。所以如果没有功能和能力，把它做得安全可靠又有什么意义？根本没人会在意。所以显然，AI 的第一要务是证明它能做一些有用的事，对吧？而它在六个月前真的达到了那个点。所以现在它真的想要被部署，被广泛部署。因此毫无疑问，整个行业现在都有一种战略上的紧迫要求，一种极其强烈的紧迫感，要确保我们部署的任何东西都是安全可靠的。所以我认为每个人都完全认同：能力、功能、安全、可靠——它们都处在完全相同的位置。

turns.en: Priority number one.
turns.zh: 头号优先事项。

turns.en: And so the question is winning. I would reframe winning—not of the technology industry winning, not of just the AI industry winning. America winning means every industry in America winning. Healthcare.
turns.zh: 所以问题在于“赢”。我会重新定义“赢”——不是科技行业赢，不只是 AI 行业赢。美国赢意味着美国每一个行业都赢。医疗。

turns.en: That's right. Nothing would give me more joy.
turns.zh: 没错。没有什么比这更让我高兴的了。

turns.en: The definition of America winning is when we talk about Lilly winning, Walmart winning, FedEx winning, every single one, Boeing winning, the US military winning,
turns.zh: 美国赢的定义就是当我们谈到礼来赢、沃尔玛赢、联邦快递赢，每一个都赢，波音赢、美国军队赢，

turns.en: every citizen winning,
turns.zh: 每个公民都赢，

turns.en: every citizen winning. And so our universities winning, our high schools winning. That's the definition of winning. There is no winning if it's just a technology that won.
turns.zh: 每个公民都赢。还有我们的大学赢、我们的高中赢。这才是赢的定义。如果只是技术赢了，那根本不算赢。

turns.en: Exactly. But nobody used it.
turns.zh: 正是如此。但没人用它。

turns.en: Right. What the greatest risk is, of course—I'll just say baseline—there will be no AI technology industry if we don't build it safely and securely. Okay, this is an existential issue for us. And if we make it an existential industry for everybody else, well, that's not going to happen, because it'll be an existential issue for us first, right? So having said that, the definition of winning for us—and this is the part I always have to change a little bit—
turns.zh: 对。最大的风险当然是——我就直说底线——如果我们不把它做得安全可靠，就不会有 AI 技术行业。好吧，这对我们来说是一个生死攸关的问题。如果我们让它成为其他所有人的生死攸关的行业，那不会发生，因为它首先会是我们的生死攸关的问题，对吧？所以话虽如此，对我们来说赢的定义——这是我总得稍微改一改的部分——

turns.en: Right?
turns.zh: 对吧？

turns.en: I want us to pivot.
turns.zh: 我想让我们转变一下。

turns.en: I like that.
turns.zh: 我喜欢这个说法。

turns.en: I want us to pivot. And when I see AI winning, America AI winning, I'm looking down from—you know, these days we spend a lot of time in the air and we're looking down. Every state's winning, every county is winning, every community is winning, every company's winning. Everybody won because we could afford to spend more on healthcare. We could afford to spend more on education. We could afford to spend more on interstate commerce, highways, etc., all of the infrastructure of the country.
turns.zh: 我想让我们转变一下。当我看到 AI 赢、美国 AI 赢时，我是从高处往下看——你知道，这些天我们花很多时间在空中，我们往下看。每个州都赢，每个县都赢，每个社区都赢，每个公司都赢。每个人都赢了，因为我们能负担得起在医疗上花更多钱。我们能负担得起在教育上花更多钱。我们能负担得起在州际商业、高速公路等等，这个国家所有基础设施上花更多钱。

turns.en: What I hear you saying is the definition of winning is that when we look back 25, 30, 40 years from now, the economy needs to be 10 times as large. Everybody's lives need to be better, and existential and primary to all of that is it has to be done in a way that's aligned with human interest. Which—this is the last question I have on this and I know we have a lot to get to. Most people don't understand what our security framework is in the country. I've said we have the most robust super intelligent security framework in the world. We're clearly the only country on the planet that's actually sanctioned a model and pulled it off the shelf with Mythos earlier this year. But I describe it as a three-legged stool. We have the frontier model review of every new frontier model by Casey and the Department of Commerce. So they do all their work. If a new model's coming out, they review it. They test it for whether or not they think it's going to cause a problem in the marketplace. Now we have the White House accord on super intelligence that you helped to architect—internal and external audits, board oversight and all of the liability that comes with that. And then third we have the SI force now led by Jay Clayton, of course Emil and Scott and Andrew, and that's doing critical industry coordination, cyber, etc. So these three legs on the stool. There are people out there—I heard Gates recently saying, 'We're not doing enough. We need new laws on the books and everything else.' That three-legged stool seems like a lot to me in a very short period of time that's come together. As a leader of one of the most important companies obviously in super intelligence, do you feel comfortable for that future that we're trying to usher in, that that is a good step forward, where we need to be right now?
turns.zh: 我听到你说的是，赢的定义就是当我们 25 年、30 年、40 年后回头看时，经济规模需要扩大 10 倍。每个人的生活都需要更好，而所有这一切的根本和首要前提是，必须以符合人类利益的方式来做。这是我在这个问题上的最后一个问题，我知道我们还有很多要聊的。大多数人并不了解我们国家的安全框架。我说过我们拥有世界上最健全的超级智能安全框架。我们显然是地球上唯一一个真正制裁过一个模型并在今年早些时候把 Mythos 下架的国家。但我把它描述成一个三条腿的凳子。第一条腿是 Casey 和商务部对每一个新的前沿模型进行前沿模型审查。他们做所有的工作。如果有新模型要发布，他们会审查它。他们会测试它，判断它是否会在市场上造成问题。第二条腿是我们现在有了关于超级智能的白宫协议，是你帮助架构的——内部和外部审计、董事会监督以及随之而来的所有责任。第三条腿是我们现在有了由 Jay Clayton 领导的 SI force，当然还有 Emil、Scott 和 Andrew，它正在做关键的行业协调、网络安全等等。所以这就是凳子上的三条腿。外面有人——我最近听到盖茨说，‘我们做得不够。我们需要制定新的法律等等。’在我看来，这第三条腿在很短的时间内就凝聚起来了，已经很多了。作为显然处于超级智能领域最重要公司之一的领导者，你对我们要引领的那个未来感到安心吗？这是向前迈出的好一步，是我们现在需要达到的位置吗？

turns.en: Yeah. The best way to get to the future is to take action quickly. And if we argue about what is perfect versus what's first, we'll end up arguing about perfection and we'll never get there. And so I love the fact that these three-legged stool are actionable. They're tangible. They have real teeth.
turns.zh: 是的。通往未来的最好方式就是迅速采取行动。如果我们争论什么是完美的、什么是先做的，我们最终会一直在争论完美，永远到不了那里。所以我喜欢这个三条腿的凳子是可执行的。它们是实实在在的。它们有真正的约束力。

turns.en: Happening now.
turns.zh: 正在发生。

turns.en: It's happening right now. You could—we're doing it now. We're taking action now. And the reason we're taking action now is because it's good for our company. It's good for our industry. It's good for our country. It's good for our society. It's good all the way around. And if we don't do these things, the outcome is less desirable. We don't get to pursue that optimistic future that we all dreamt about.
turns.zh: 它正在发生。你可以——我们现在就在做。我们现在就在采取行动。我们现在采取行动的原因是，这对我们的公司有好处。对我们的行业有好处。对我们的国家有好处。对我们的社会有好处。方方面面都有好处。如果我们不做这些事，结果就不那么理想。我们就无法去追求我们所有人都梦想过的那个乐观的未来。

turns.en: And so if you go back and look at another industry, I don't remember another industry that is as it's currently at its current state, right? And have now formulated all of these cross-company, cross-industrial, government-to-industry coordination to make sure that we advance this in a responsible and optimistic way.
turns.zh: 如果你回顾另一个行业，我不记得有哪个行业像现在这样处于当前状态，对吧？并且现在已经制定了所有这些跨公司、跨行业、政府与行业的协调，以确保我们以负责任和乐观的方式推进这件事。

turns.en: Yeah. I just think it's so important for people to understand because when I hear senators talking about it on television on both sides to be perfectly honest, like they don't—they have to learn about what we're doing here. They don't even know what we're doing, right? Like we are doing an extraordinary amount, and by the way, these aren't voluntary things. There's not going to be a frontier model that gets released that Casey is not reviewing and the Commerce Department is not reviewing, and they've demonstrated they have the authority under export controls to pull them off the shelf.
turns.zh: 是的。我只是觉得让人们理解这一点非常重要，因为当我在电视上听到两边参议员谈论这件事时，说实话，他们并不——他们必须了解我们在这里做什么。他们甚至不知道我们在做什么，对吧？比如我们正在做大量非凡的工作，而且顺便说一句，这些不是自愿的事情。不会有一个前沿模型发布时 Casey 不审查、商务部不审查，而且他们已经证明根据出口管制他们有权将其下架。

turns.en: Do two things: one, come and spend some time and learn what actually has to be done. What's the problem, right? If you want a solution, you got to at least understand what the problem is. Right.
turns.zh: 做两件事：第一，来花些时间了解实际需要做什么。问题是什么，对吧？如果你想要解决方案，你至少得理解问题是什么。对吧。

turns.en: Right. And so one, come and just learn about—we got plenty of time. I got all the time in the world for this kind of stuff. And just, you know, come talk to us. Come talk to our industry and learn. The second thing is learn about the solution that we put in place and then try to see if we can make that—if there are ideas to make that better. Of course, we're all completely open-minded, right? But be constructive, right?
turns.zh: 对。所以第一，来了解一下——我们有很多时间。我对这类事情有的是时间。就，你知道，来和我们谈谈。来和我们的行业谈谈，学习一下。第二件事是了解我们制定的解决方案，然后试着看看我们能否让它——如果有想法让它更好。当然，我们全都完全持开放态度，对吧？但要建设性，对吧？

turns.en: I thought that was part of the fourth point on the accord on superintelligence—was this is not static, this is dynamic. This group is going to get together routinely, we're going to update the framework as required when the technology evolves. But I want to move forward now to compute. Of course, long-running agents that work in teams of thousands or millions to solve complicated tasks—it all consumes massively more compute. Dylan, our friend at SemiAnalysis, has said we're going to bring on board 43 gigawatts of new AI compute next year. Just to contextualize it, we'll share a chart with people online—that's more than all of the AI compute that exists in the world today. So we're going to bring that on board next year. The year after that, another 40 gigawatts of compute. You are the one—you know where every single GPU is allocated, right? So as you sit here, does that sound right to you? Do you think we're going to bring on that much compute? And do you think that some of the things we're hearing out there about permitting issues or bottlenecks in the supply chain or pro-local protests—do you think the number is going to be materially different than that based upon what you're seeing?
turns.zh: 我认为那是超级智能协议第四点的一部分——这不是静态的，这是动态的。这个小组会定期聚在一起，当技术发展时我们会根据需要更新框架。但我想现在转向算力。当然，长时间运行的智能体以数千或数百万的团队协作解决复杂任务——这一切都消耗大量更多的算力。我们的朋友、SemiAnalysis 的 Dylan 说过，明年我们将新增 43 吉瓦的新 AI 算力。为了让大家有个概念，我们会在网上分享一张图表——这比当今世界上所有 AI 算力加起来还多。所以明年我们将新增这么多。后年再新增 40 吉瓦算力。你是那个知道每一块 GPU 分配在哪里的人，对吧？所以当你坐在这里，这听起来对吗？你觉得我们会新增那么多算力吗？你觉得我们听到的一些关于许可问题、供应链瓶颈或支持本地的抗议——根据你所看到的，你觉得这个数字会与此有实质性不同吗？

turns.en: I think the demand is definitely there and more.
turns.zh: 我认为需求肯定存在，而且更多。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: The demand is definitely there and more. The challenge, of course, is that there are a lot of obstacles when you move from digital to the physical. There are a lot of obstacles there. Land permitting. There's power generation that you've got to bring online. Of course, you need construction workers and outfitters and plumbers and, you know, all kinds of—created a million new jobs just building these things. Create a million new jobs, and their skills are not fungible. You know, they have a lot of skills, and particularly the ones that are building these $50 billion data centers. You're going to want some people with great skills, and there's a critical part of every single one of the buildouts of these things where you need some very specific skills. And so I think that—and then there's, of course, whatever moratoriums that are happening, whatever issues that we're seeing around the country. And so I think this is—my guess is that land, power, shell, the buildout resources will be one of the most important obstacles to reaching that.
turns.zh: 需求肯定存在，而且更多。当然，挑战在于当你从数字世界转向物理世界时，有很多障碍。那里有很多障碍。土地许可。你必须上线发电。当然，你需要建筑工人、装配工、水管工，你知道，各种各样的——仅仅建造这些东西就创造了上百万个新工作岗位。创造上百万个新工作岗位，而他们的技能不是可替代的。你知道，他们有很多技能，尤其是那些建造这些 500 亿美元数据中心的人。你会想要一些技能出色的人，而且每一个这类建设都有一个关键部分，你需要一些非常具体的技能。所以我认为——然后当然还有正在发生的任何暂停令，我们在全国各地看到的任何问题。所以我认为这是——我的猜测是，土地、电力、外壳、建设资源将是达到那个目标的最重要障碍之一。

turns.en: And so our company, as you know, now speaking specifically for us, there are several things that we're doing to mitigate that. And one, you know, because we're the only company that serves every CSP, we serve every NCP. We have great enterprise businesses through Dell and HP and Lenovo and others. And because we serve every single industry and we're across the entire life cycle of AI—everything from, you know, of course data processing to training to post-training to inference to agentic processing, and all of the tool use that we accelerate—you know, our exposure to our go-to-market is the largest of all. Every contract manufacturer in the world is working on my behalf. Every go-to-market is connected to our architecture. And so if one particular state, one particular community, one particular data center has a hard time, right, you know, our demand is so much greater than our supply at the moment, we'll just adjust our supply chain accordingly.
turns.zh: 所以我们的公司，如你所知，现在具体说我们，我们正在做几件事来缓解这个问题。第一，你知道，因为我们是唯一一家服务所有 CSP 的公司，我们服务所有 NCP。我们通过 Dell、HP、Lenovo 等拥有伟大的企业业务。而且因为我们服务每一个行业，我们横跨 AI 的整个生命周期——从你知道的当然数据处理到训练到后训练到推理到智能体式处理，以及我们加速的所有工具使用——你知道，我们的市场覆盖是最大的。世界上每一家合同制造商都在为我工作。每一个市场渠道都连接到我们的架构。所以如果某个特定的州、某个特定的社区、某个特定的数据中心遇到困难，对吧，你知道，目前我们的需求远大于供应，我们只需相应调整我们的供应链。

turns.en: The other thing that we have—and I don't love this answer as much—but as you know, Nvidia is also the infrastructure for the planet. And so whether it's in Europe or—and we've got early developments now in Africa, in Central Asia, in Southeast Asia and Latin America, in the Middle East, and so on and so forth. And so I don't love that the United States can't keep up.
turns.zh: 我们有的另一件事——我不那么喜欢这个答案——但如你所知，Nvidia 也是这个星球的基础设施。所以无论是在欧洲还是——我们现在在非洲、中亚、东南亚和拉丁美洲、中东等地都有早期发展。所以我不喜欢美国跟不上。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: But for our business specifically, we have such a global reach, and there's buildout demand all around the world. If we don't build it out here, you know, I think we just all have to recognize that every country in the world would love to have it built out there.
turns.zh: 但具体到我们的业务，我们拥有如此全球化的覆盖，全世界都有建设需求。如果我们不在这里建设，你知道，我想我们都必须认识到，世界上每个国家都希望在那里建设。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And so I think that our business specifically is probably the most resilient. And the reason for that is all the things that I mentioned—you know, we cover the entire spectrum of AI. tldr.zh: 推理需要海量算力，计算需求将增长十亿倍。

tldr.en: Perfect alignment is impossible; containment and monitoring ensure safety.
tldr.zh: 完美对齐不可能，安全靠围堵与监控。

tldr.en: Moore's law is over; doubling transistors now costs double, not the same price.
tldr.zh: 摩尔定律已终结，晶体管翻倍成本也翻倍。

qs.en: Why will compute demand explode a billion times?
qs.zh: 为什么计算需求会爆炸式增长十亿倍？

qs.en: How do we ensure safety if alignment is impossible?
qs.zh: 如果对齐不可能，我们如何确保安全？

qs.en: Is Nvidia's moat increasing with scale?
qs.zh: 英伟达的护城河会随规模扩大而加深吗？
